rationale: flops-6 is a tiny, call-free, global-free floating-point kernel dominated by a hot arithmetic loop, so passes that transform arithmetic and control flow inside functions are the best fit while call/global-oriented passes are useless: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because the dense FP expression chains are exactly what arithmetic substitution obscures best (with a modest CorrectnessRisk weight to reflect FP rounding sensitivity), FLA and BCF provide strong structural resistance but their RuntimeCost weights are kept moderate-to-elevated since any branch overhead multiplies across the hot loop, SPLIT is cheap and low-risk so it is freely enabled to feed better inputs to FLA, IBR is enabled with a higher RuntimeCost weight so it is applied sparingly where branch-density features justify it, and ICALL and IGV are omitted entirely because the program has essentially no indirect calls or global variable tables for them to hide, so they would add overhead and complexity with zero security return.
